clustered-settlement.def: A rural settlement pattern in which homes are grouped together in a village, with farmland around it; also called nucleated settlement.

dispersed-settlement.def: A rural settlement pattern in which homes are spread out, usually one farmhouse on each farm, as in the US Midwest.

linear-settlement.def: A rural settlement pattern in which homes line up along a road, river, canal or coast, as along the Nile in Egypt.

metes-and-bounds.def: A survey method that marks land by distances and by natural or human features such as streams, trees and walls, giving irregular parcels; used in the eastern United States.

township-and-range.def: A survey method that divides land into a grid of townships 6 miles square, each with 36 sections of 1 square mile; set up by the US Land Ordinance of 1785.

long-lot.def: A survey method that divides land into long, narrow strips running back from a river, so each owner has river frontage; used by French settlers in Quebec and Louisiana.
